message.content: Pandas belong to the order Carnivora, but they diverged from other carnivores early on. Their lineage split from the common ancestor of bears (family Ursidae) around 20–25 million years ago. Fossil evidence shows that the earliest known panda relatives were small, omnivorous mammals that lived in forested environments. Over time, the giant panda evolved specialized bamboo‑feeding adaptations—such as a pseudo‑thumb formed by an enlarged wrist bone—to exploit abundant bamboo resources in the temperate forests of China. The modern giant panda (Ailuropoda melanoleuca) emerged roughly 2–3 million years ago, with its distinctive black‑and‑white coat and highly selective diet becoming fully established by the Pleistocene.
